audit_findings.title: Loan-book reinvestment may be missing from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.656 million net cash use across consumer, MHP and dealer loan activity in 2025; $12.058 million net cash use in the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Required loan-book investment reduces distributable owner earnings; omitting it capitalizes lending income without the capital needed to sustain that income.
audit_findings.evidence: Consumer, MHP and dealer loans interest income increased $2.5 million, or 6.1%, from 2024 to 2025 due to growth in our loan portfolios.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate recurring capital movement through the operating loan portfolios, but the record does not establish whether the OE workpapers deduct the maintenance portion. The first-half 2026 net use equals 28.7% of the $42.0 million annual anchor, so a sustained omission could materially reduce the valuation. Growth originations must be separated from maintenance reinvestment before adjusting OE.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile annual originations, principal collections, charge-offs and repossession costs by portfolio to the OE workpapers; calculate maintenance loan-book reinvestment and rerun every scenario if it is absent.

audit_findings.title: A concentrated $48.6 million note reached maturity after the bridge date
audit_findings.magnitude: $46.6 million principal remaining after the filed $2.0 million payment, equal to 7.5% of the $619 million base equity value; old contractual annual interest was approximately $3.84 million
audit_findings.mechanism: A loss or nonaccrual would reduce equity capital and owner earnings, while modified terms could change recurring interest income and the sustainable OE anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: As consideration under the Agreement, the Makers conveyed to the Company clear title to the Forest Hollow Mobile Home Community in Beaumont, Texas and the Cleveland Mobile Home Community in Richland, Mississippi, together with related personal property and intangible assets, and the parties executed a new $ 48.6 million promissory note (the “New Note”) bearing a fixed interest rate of 7.9 %, requiring monthly interest-only payments for twenty-four months and maturing in July 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated adverse credit event, not merely a possibility: the note was not repaid in full at maturity and entered forbearance and modification. Additional collateral and guarantees may protect recovery, but no independent collateral coverage or executed final documentation establishes collectability. The remaining exposure is large enough to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the executed modification, post-maturity payment history, lien and guaranty verification, independent collateral appraisals and borrower financials; rerun the valuation for supported loss, nonaccrual and revised-interest outcomes.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may include customer escrow owed ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $14.554 million maximum June 30, 2026 escrow overlap, equal to $0.61 per share and 2.4% of the $619 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any escrow-funded cash must be excluded from the cash bridge because the corresponding amount belongs to customers rather than common shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: The liabilities associated with these escrow collections totaled $ 13.1 million and $ 11.6 million as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, and are included in escrow liability in the accompanying balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes a $14.554 million escrow liability but does not establish how much of the $28.965 million cash balance is escrow-funded. Even treating the entire liability as unavailable would reduce base value from $25.98 to approximately $25.37 per share and bull value from $30.43 to approximately $29.82; the market price of $28.41 would remain above base value and below bull value. This bounded correction therefore does not change the stated valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile June 30 bank accounts and restricted or escrow balances to the escrow liability, then replace gross cash with shareholder-available cash in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The anchor and bridge use different acquisition perimeters
audit_findings.magnitude: $19.868 million purchase consideration; only $1.0 million revenue and a $28 thousand pre-tax loss were included for two months of 2025; full-year effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A full post-acquisition perimeter can change normalized OE, maintenance reinvestment and the liabilities or assets incorporated into the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2025, our statement of income included total revenue of $ 1.0 million and pre-tax loss of $ 28 from the AmeriCasa Acquisition.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but the two-month contribution does not measure AmeriCasa's normalized annual economics. The 2026 consolidated filing does not isolate its earnings or cash requirements, and pending litigation and provisional acquisition accounting further obscure the effect. The direction and materiality therefore cannot be established from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a twelve-month post-acquisition standalone income and cash-reinvestment schedule, reconcile acquired receivables and obligations, incorporate finalized purchase-price accounting and litigation developments, and rerun the valuation on a consistent perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Material control weaknesses reduce confidence in the lending and acquisition inputs
audit_findings.mechanism: Undetected errors could affect the OE anchor, loan-loss provisions, acquisition accounting, taxes, shares or balance-sheet bridge amounts.
audit_findings.evidence: In our opinion, because of the effect of the material weaknesses identified below on the achievement of the objectives of the control criteria, the Company has not maintained effective internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025, based on criteria established in Internal Control-Integrated Framework (2013) issued by COSO.
audit_findings.explanation: The adverse internal-control opinion and continued June 2026 weaknesses are demonstrated, but they do not establish a specific misstatement. The unqualified 2025 financial-statement opinion provides countervailing assurance for the annual figures, while the latest quarter remains unaudited. Without identified input errors, valuation magnitude and direction cannot be quantified.
audit_findings.action: Tie every valuation input to audited schedules or subsequent cash realization; independently test loan allowances, repossessed assets, AmeriCasa balances, tax items and June-quarter liabilities before relying on the current valuation.

audit_findings.title: Existing dealer profit-sharing obligations may be absent from prospective cash flows
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.800 million liability at June 30, 2026, equal to $0.08 per share and 0.3% of the $619 million base equity value; first-half 2026 liability reduction was $1.006 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Settlement of previously accrued dealer incentives consumes cash without a second income-statement expense, so an earnings-only OE forecast can omit the working-capital outflow.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, the dealer incentive liability was $ 2.8 million and $ 4.4 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates the obligation and its cash-flow movement, but even deducting the entire June balance immediately would reduce base value by only about $0.08 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion. Recurring dealer-incentive expense remains in reported earnings; the open issue is principally settlement timing.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that OE captures dealer-incentive settlements or liability changes and reconcile the June 2026 balance to projected portfolio collections; correct the cash-flow schedule if omitted.
